history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the town is not 'Udupi' but Anegudde (also called Kumbashi), a village in Kundapura taluk of Udupi district, ~9 km south of Kundapura and ~30 km north of Udupi. This is one of the most visited Ganesha temples in coastal Karnataka, reckoned among the seven 'Mukti Sthalas' of Parashurama Kshetra and part of Tulunadu's Sapthakshetra. According to legend, when drought struck the region, sage Agasthya performed a yagna that the demon Kumbhasura kept disrupting; the sage sought help from the Pandavas, and Bhima — after praying to Ganesha, who appeared in the guise of an elephant and gave him a sword (asi) — slew the demon. Hence 'Kumbh-asi' became Kumbhashi/Kumbashi, while 'Anegudde' means the hillock of the elephant god (aane = elephant, gudde = hillock). The deity is a ~12-foot tall standing idol of Sri Siddhi Vinayaka carved from a single stone and covered in silver armour; a four-armed form with two hands in varada hasta and two pointing to his feet as a means to salvation. The reported age of the temple (1,200 vs 1,500 years in different sources) rests on tradition, not verified epigraphy.

name: Anegudde Vinayaka Temple
town_description: Anegudde, also known as Kumbashi, is a temple village in Kundapura taluk of Udupi district on NH-66, about 9 km south of Kundapura town and roughly 30 km north of Udupi city. Surrounded by lush greenery with sacred tanks (Surya and Chandra Pushkarinis), it is a busy pilgrimage stop for travellers on the coastal highway. Nearby shrines include the Mahalingeshwara temple and a branch of the Sode Matha.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism-adjacent Ganesha worship; Vaishnavite legends of Tulunadu)
